text: in patterns of infection and drug resistance: • WHO: for chlamydial epididymitis: • oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days, or • a single dose of oral azithromycin 1 g alternatives, given for 7 days, are: • oral amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily • oral erythromycin 500 mg four times daily • oral ofloxacin 300 mg twice daily • oral tetracycline 500 mg four times daily Unless it can be excluded, patients should also be treated concurrently for gonorrhoea (p.191). • UK: for probable chlamydial infections or infections with other non-gonococcal, non-enteric organisms: • oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 10 to 14 days is rec- ommended for infections with enteric organisms: • oral ofloxacin 200 mg twice daily for 14 days, or • oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily for 10 days for disease most probably due to gonococcal infection: • a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone 250 mg, or • a single oral dose of ciprofloxacin 500 mg plus oral doxycy- cline 100 mg twice daily for 10 to 14 days in patients allergic to cephalosporins and/or tetracy- clines infections from all causes may be treated with: • oral ofloxacin 200 mg twice daily for 14 days • USA: empirical treatment recommended: likely cause gonococcal or chlamydial infection: • a single intramuscular dose of ceftriaxone 250 mg plus oral doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 10 days likely cause an enteric organism or in patients allergic to cephalosporins and/or tetracyclines: • oral ofloxacin 300 mg twice daily for 10 days, or • oral levofloxacin 500 mg once daily for 10 days Sexual contacts should also be treated if epididymitis is caused by a sexually transmitted pathogen.2,3 Patients co-infected with HIV should receive the same treatment as those who are HIV-negative.3 1.
